rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 line 6: 'This is a 1983 argument, not an AI take.' — cataphoric 'This' resolves within the same bullet (continues 'Lisanne Bainbridge... the human keeps exactly two jobs'). Line 7 'Both jobs' -> 'exactly two jobs' named line 6, same chunk. Chunk 2 line 13 'named this **overreliance**: trusting the machine...' — 'this' resolved by the immediately following colon-clause in the same sentence. Chunk 2 line 14 'the agent' (first literal appearance in this file) has no in-file antecedent, but is arc-earned spine vocabulary for the whole AE101 training: verified via grep that 'the agent' is plain body vocabulary from M1 onward (`getting-going.md` lines 17, 33, 57), and this lecture sits at the M4 close, several modules downstream — per check_slides.md's arc-earned-spine-vocabulary carve-out, it does not need re-introduction on this slide. Closest-to-violating candidate: chunk 2 line 15 'The trust... The watching' — both resolve cleanly to 'trust'/'vigilance' named in the header (line 10) and prior bullets, no gap.

Scanned every sentence in lines 1-16: no phrase points at another file or names a prior slide/lecture by position (no 'the opening lecture said', 'that story', etc.). All callbacks are within-file (header -> bullet) or attribute Bainbridge/Parasuraman-Riley by name, which is citation, not a positional callback. No candidate even approaches this rule.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 (lines 3-9) carries 3 substantive bullets on the two-job mechanism; chunk 2 (lines 10-16) carries 3 substantive bullets on the trust/vigilance mechanism. Neither is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Chunk 0 (line 1) is the title-only lede, exempt as the title slide by the template's own chunk-0 convention.

Chunk 1 header 'Monitoring and takeover run on the same reps' (line 3) is proven by its own content (lines 6-8): two jobs, monitor and take over, both riding on reps that daily automation removes. Chunk 2 header 'Trust and vigilance move in opposite directions' (line 10) is restated near-verbatim as the chunk's own line 15 — the strongest possible self-carry, no contradiction in either chunk.

Checked all sub-items across lines 1-16: (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction — zero instances. (b) anaphora/epistrophe triples — closest candidate is line 6's pair 'Monitor for the rare failure. Take over when it happens.', a pair not a triple; no triple found anywhere. (c) self-grading superlatives / value-prop leak — none; the file never grades its own usefulness. (d) number + own retraction — the only number present is '1983' (line 6), a plain citation date, never hedged or retracted. (e) abstraction-noun stacks — 'hands-on fluency' (line 7) and 'detection performance' (line 13) are the closest candidates but are ordinary terms carried from the cited literature, not invented noun-stacking. (f) empty-leg verb triplets — none; longest verb chain is the two-verb 'Monitor... Take over' (line 6).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture file, so both `##` headings must be claims, not imperatives/labels. Line 3 'Monitoring and takeover run on the same reps' and line 10 'Trust and vigilance move in opposite directions' are both full declarative sentences stating the slide's law. Neither is an orientation-header or catalogue-entry exemption case; both are load-bearing claims the chunk content proves out (cross-checked against rule 6).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked each of the 6 body bullets (lines 6-8, 13-15) against the three low-value classes. None is a doctrine-restatement of a repo-vocabulary split/lens/law announced with nothing added; none is self-referential design commentary about the curriculum being a pedagogy; none is an aphorism-kicker restating the header with nothing else attached. Closest-to-violating: line 15 opens with 'Trust and vigilance move in opposite directions' — a near-verbatim echo of the chunk-2 header (line 10) — but the same bullet continues into the load-bearing reframe ('The trust is deserved. The watching still has to be engineered.') and the lecture's one closing question, which the backing block names as 'the design's own move, and deliberately the only thing the opener asks the student to do' — so the bullet as a whole earns its slot even though its opening clause echoes the header.
